subject: Next steps: PR creation & Coupa/Ariba supplier ID linkage for Redwood pilot

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: PR creation & Coupa/Ariba supplier ID linkage for Redwood pilot

Thanks again for your time today, Sara — good conversation and appreciate the transparency on procurement timelines. Short recap + proposed next steps so procurement has what they need to move forward.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Goal: 30-day pilot for three internal teams to validate latency/cost tradeoffs, then expand.
- Commercial path: Acme prefers PO via Coupa if possible; card is only for one-off sandbox purchases.
- Procurement constraints: Supplier onboarding + supplier ID required before PR creation; vendor docs (W9, COI) may be requested.
- Marketplace interest: Team asked whether Redwood is available in any marketplaces (AWS, Azure) — helpful but not required for initial PR.

What we need from Acme to create the PR:
1) Confirm procurement path: Coupa PR (preferred) or Ariba?
2) If Coupa: send your buyer team name and internal project code to include on the PR.
3) If marketplace is required, let us know so we can prioritize marketplace listing (2–3 week lead time).
4) Any internal ticketing number for supplier onboarding (please paste so we can reference).

What Redwood will provide:
- Attached: Redwood_PR_Instructions_v1.pdf (step-by-step for PR creation) and Sample_PO_Template.xlsx.
- If you need a supplier ID for initial PR, Redwood can provide a temporary vendor code to expedite procurement while marketplace work is underway.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (technical) and Neha (contracts) to help with any vendor paperwork or acceptance criteria for the pilot.

Proposed next step: a short procurement enablement call (20 min) with your procurement/finance buyer + our procurement/finance owner. I’m available Thu 2/19 10–12 PT or Tue 2/24 9–11 PT — which works for your team?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0172

Attachments: Redwood_PR_Instructions_v1.pdf, Sample_PO_Template.xlsx

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the docs. Helpful. A couple quick updates from our side: 

- Procurement confirmed they will use Coupa and will require Redwood's supplier/vendor ID for the PR.
- Procurement will also need standard vendor paperwork (W9 + COI).
- Our procurement team uses an internal ticket tracker — they asked for a vendor onboarding reference ID so they can attach the paperwork.

Can you provide Redwood's supplier ID and an internal reference we can use? If you don’t have a permanent supplier ID in Coupa yet, a temporary vendor code would be fine for the PR so we can get the pilot ordered.

Maya (cc) is our finance lead who will own the PR. We should include the project code: ACME-RED-2026 in the PR.

Also, please confirm whether Redwood is already listed on any marketplaces (AWS Marketplace or Azure). If so, our procurement would prefer that path — otherwise Coupa is acceptable.

Thanks,

Thanks, Sara — looping in the key procurement/ops details below to make this straightforward for your buyer team.

Short answers:
- Redwood is not yet on AWS Marketplace for the managed pilot SKU — marketplace listing is possible but is a separate process (est. 2–3 weeks). For the pilot, Coupa PR is the fastest route.
- Temporary supplier/vendor code we can provide for the PR: RW-TMP-3819. This will allow your team to create the PR while we complete vendor onboarding.
- Permanent supplier ID (will be created during vendor onboarding): RW-3819 (we’ll confirm final ID once the supplier packet is processed).

Procurement checklist for a Coupa PR:
1) Create PR referencing vendor code RW-TMP-3819 (or RW-3819 if onboarding completes first).
2) Include project code: ACME-RED-2026 and your internal cost center.
3) Attach Sample_PO_Template.xlsx (attached to Marissa's note) and note pilot term (30 days, SKU: REDWOOD-PILOT-30).
4) Procurement should upload vendor docs (W9, COI) to their supplier onboarding ticket and cc neha_kapoor@redwood.com.

If you prefer Ariba, the flow is similar — we just need your buyer's Ariba supplier request form, and Neha can coordinate the acceptance criteria.

Mutual action plan (to attach in HubSpot):
- 0–2 days: Procurement creates PR using RW-TMP-3819 and routes for approval. (Owner: Acme procurement)
- 0–5 days: Redwood provides vendor documents (W9, COI) and confirms invoice remit details. (Owner: Neha)
- 1–7 days: PR approved and PO issued; Redwood issues invoice per PO terms and pilot onboarding begins.

Internal ticket references we can use: Supplier onboarding ticket SVC-5231 (Redwood internal) — please include this in the PR notes so our ops team can prioritize. I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543 for reference.

Happy to join the procurement call — Marissa, I can be there at any time you propose.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
